newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX falls below 5,000 points.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX falls below 5,000 points.

text.p: The Hungarian share market fell across-the-board on Friday pulling the BUX index below 5,000 points for the first time in two months.
The BUX index finished at 4,992.45 points, down 126.15. The last day when the BUX was below 5,000 points, was on January 15, when it closed at 4,925.25.
Traders said growing expectations of an interest rate rise in the U.S. may have encouraged foreign investors to reduce their exposure to stock markets.
"Expectations of an interest rate rise have grown and foreigners may have cut off their share portfolio," said Robert Forgo of MKB Securities.
Traders said that Wall Street's plunge on Thursday reinforced the downward correction of the Hungarian stock exchange and will remain the determining factor in the short term.
"The fall on Wall Street has amplified the correction," one trader said earlier.
"(Friday's) Dow Jones index will determine the Hungarian market's direction on Monday," Forgo said.

Only a handful of stocks bucked the slide on Friday, including tile manufacturer Zalakeramia, which gained 100 forints to end at 8,300, after announcing it had acquired a majority stake in Hungarian tile maker Pietra, its second purchase since the end of February.
Chemicals maker Borsodchem, rated by Postabank Securities as 'buy', dipped 50 forints to finish at 5,950.
Gas distributor Primagaz which said it would propose the payout of a 17.5 percent dividend on 1996 results, compared to 15 percent last year, fell 350 forints to 8,250.
Chemicals TVK and oil company MOL were more in focus, as both of them broke a support level of 2,000 forints and 3,000 forints, respectively.
TVK closed at 1,945 forints, down 105, while MOL at 2,985, down 15.
